title: 800 Women in Pink Sarees, a 60-Foot Waterfall Poster, and the Dhamaal Boys Are Coming for July
excerpt: Dhamaal 4 is pulling out every trick in the Bollywood promotion playbook — and it hasn't even released yet. Here's why the franchise's wildest chapter might also be its biggest.
body:
There is a very specific kind of insanity that only the **Dhamaal** franchise can get away with. Not the polished, carefully art-directed chaos of a Marvel launch. Not the solemn press-conference gravitas of a prestige drama. This is the kind of madness where someone looks at a 60-foot waterfall and says, *"What if we drop a movie poster down that?"* — and everyone in the room just nods.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=IG-eByZdz6Y</youtube>

That is exactly what happened on June 12, when the trailer of **Dhamaal 4** was launched at Imagicaa, Mumbai's beloved amusement park, with the entire star cast in attendance. A massive poster cascaded down a grand waterfall while the assembled media were taken on an immersive, adventure-style experience that mirrored the film's treasure-hunt narrative. It was promotional filmmaking at its most gleefully unhinged — and it set the tone for what has become one of the most entertaining marketing campaigns in recent Bollywood memory.

## The Saree That Broke the Mall

Then came Saturday, June 27. A Thane mall. **Riteish Deshmukh** and newcomer **Anjali Anand**. And 800 women dressed head to toe in pink sarees.

The occasion was the launch of *'Saree'*, the newest track from the Dhamaal 4 soundtrack — a peppy, irresistible Hindi reimagining of the iconic Marathi song *'Gulabi Sadi'* by **Sanju Rathod**. With music by **Tanishk Bagchi** and Rathod himself, the song bridges two worlds: the viral, emotionally charged Marathi original and the broad, multiplatform appeal of a Bollywood franchise soundtrack.

> "When the makers approached me to sing Saree for Dhamaal 4, I was genuinely thrilled. Dhamaal is such a loved franchise, so being associated with it is a very special feeling for me." — Sanju Rathod

The visual — Riteish and Anjali performing the track live while surrounded by a sea of pink — was designed for virality, and it delivered. In Lokmat's production partnership, it became one of those real-world moments that look better on a phone screen than they do in person, which is exactly the point.


## The Gang's All Here

For anyone who grew up on *Dhamaal* (2007), *Double Dhamaal* (2011), and *Total Dhamaal* (2019), the core appeal has never changed: four friends, one treasure, and approximately zero common sense.

**Ajay Devgn**, **Arshad Warsi**, **Riteish Deshmukh**, **Jaaved Jaaferi**, and **Sanjay Mishra** are all back. The trailer, which has already racked up solid views since its Imagicaa debut, promises another chaotic treasure hunt — this time with even higher stakes and an expanded cast that includes **Esha Gupta**, **Sanjeeda Shaikh**, **Anjali Anand**, **Upendra Limaye**, **Vijay Patkar**, and **Ravi Kishan**.

Director **Indra Kumar** has always understood something fundamental about this franchise: it is not trying to be clever. It is trying to be *fun*. And in a year where Bollywood has leaned heavily into spy thrillers, intense dramas, and emotional period pieces, that kind of unapologetic silliness is a genuine market gap.

## The Gentleman's Agreement

Behind the scenes, one of the more fascinating subplots of Dhamaal 4's journey has been its release date chess. The film was originally set for July 3 but shifted to avoid clashing with **Welcome To The Jungle**. Then it moved again, settling on **July 10**, to create breathing room before Christopher Nolan's **The Odyssey** arrives on July 17.

According to trade sources, **Ajay Devgn** and **Akshay Kumar** — two superstars who have spent decades sharing the comedy-entertainer space — had a direct conversation and agreed that releasing two large-scale comedies a week apart would cannibalise both films. The result: Welcome To The Jungle opened June 26, Dhamaal 4 arrives July 10, and The Odyssey gets a solo July 17. Everyone breathes.

It is the kind of old-school gentlemen's arrangement that used to happen all the time in Bollywood and rarely does anymore. That it happened between two of the industry's biggest names, over comedy franchises no less, says something about how seriously the business takes the summer corridor in 2026.

## What the Diaspora Should Know

Dhamaal 4 releases in cinemas worldwide on **July 10, 2026**. For NRIs in the US, UK, and Canada, the franchise has always been solid family weekend fare — the kind of film you take your parents to, or the one that settles the "what should we watch" argument in under three seconds. Expect wide international distribution through T-Series and Devgn Films.

The soundtrack is already doing numbers: *'Qeher'* by **Guru Randhawa** dropped on June 19, *'Chatni'* brought Bhojpuri flavour to the playlist, and *'Saree'* is the newest addition. All three are available on Spotify, Apple Music, JioSaavn, and YouTube Music.

With the trailer out, the music rolling, and the promotional circus in full swing, the only question left is whether Dhamaal 4 can match — or top — *Total Dhamaal*'s ₹228-crore worldwide haul from 2019. If the energy of 800 women in pink sarees is any indication, July is going to be loud.
